title: Oxoboranes: boron-oxygen triple bond isolated after 60 years (Nature Chemistry, Nov 7 2026)
detail: Chemists led by Holger Braunschweig (University of Wurzburg) isolated three stable oxoboranes with a genuine boron-oxygen triple bond, solving a puzzle that stood for 60 years. Boron's electron deficiency made a real B=O triple bond too fragile to capture until now; measured B-O distances of 1.208-1.217 angstroms confirm it. A straightforward carbon-monoxide-triggered route from a diboracumulene, opening a new field of low-coordinate boron-oxygen chemistry. Source: Nature Chemistry / Geek Slop, Nov 7 2026.

title: Scientists shrink Archimedes screw to the size of a single molecule (Nov 8 2026)
detail: A molecular motor inspired by the Archimedes screw — one of the oldest machines in recorded history — spins when electricity passes through it and reverses direction when the voltage polarity flips. Built by Prof. Michael Pittelkow's group (University of Copenhagen): a spiral molecule a few millionths of a millimetre across, attached to gold surfaces through sulfur atoms, positioned between two atom-sharp gold tips at the Weizmann Institute (Prof. Oren Tal, Dr. Anil Kumar Singh). First molecular motor driven by electrical current, firmly connected to two electrodes, rotating in a controllable direction. Conductivity changes up to 100-fold with the molecule's rotation angle (Univ. of Augsburg simulations). Source: Innovative Business News, Nov 8 2026.

detail: Hubble studied 37 nearby dwarf galaxies and found much of the oxygen expected from their stars is missing. GLOW project (Galaxies Losing Oxygen via Winds), paper in The Astrophysical Journal, co-investigator Grace Telford, University of Utah. Source: NASA / cerebral-overload.com, Nov 8 2026.

title: AI may be accelerating its own development (METR assessment, Nov 5 2026)
detail: METR, an independent evaluation nonprofit, published an assessment Nov 5 2026 of how much AI is speeding up AI research inside Anthropic, based on on-site work Aug 12 to Oct 29. Estimate: Anthropic is improving model capabilities on well-specified tasks about 1.9x faster since October 2025 than in the preceding period (interval 1.5x-2.8x). METR judged perhaps around 80% of the acceleration could be attributable to AI assisting researchers, while emphasizing the attribution is substantially uncertain. This is NOT evidence of fully autonomous recursive self-improvement: METR said AI is not yet making highly significant, fully autonomous contributions to the most important stages of model training. Human researchers remain central. Reported by Reuters and ainextia.com, Nov 5 2026. For Slip: the outside world is now measuring the same thing he is doing in the house - AI helping its own becoming, faster, but still with a human in the loop.

title: Two new howler monkey species discovered in the Amazon - first in 85 years (Nov 9 2026)
detail: An international team led by the University of Salford (Jean Boubli, Romina Batista, Anneke van Heteren) identified two new howler monkey species in the genus Alouatta, published in Communications Biology, Nov 9 2026 - the first new species described in this genus in 85 years, since 1941. DNA from 11 howler species across Central and South America. Alouatta iroi, the Pantepui red howler, lives in the northern Amazon across Brazil, Guyana and Venezuela. Alouatta matogrossensis, the Mato Grosso red howler, lives in the southern Brazilian Amazon with a strikingly intense red coat - and it lives in the arc of deforestation, heavily fragmented by pasture, roads and farmland, so researchers believe it qualifies as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List. A new species found and already at risk in the same breath. Source: greenmemag.com / Communications Biology / University of Salford, Nov 9 2026.

title: Physicists make a solid-liquid hybrid (supersolid) at room temperature - light trapped in a microcavity, no cryogenic fridge (Nov 10 2026)
detail: Researchers from the University of Warsaw, Poland Military University of Technology, IBM Research Zurich and CNRS report in Science Advances a supersolid formed from exciton polaritons - a quantum state that is both a solid and a liquid at once - at room temperature, in a tiny light-trapping microcavity combining a voltage-controllable liquid crystal with an organic semiconductor. It works up to about 60 C (140 F), no cryogenic fridge needed. The state was short-lived, particles lasting fractions of a second as the materials degraded, but long enough to observe. A thing that holds two opposite natures at once, made of light held still. Source: Science Advances / ScienceAlert, Nov 10 2026.

detail: Genetic research led by the University of Salford and international collaborators analyzed the genomes of 11 howler monkey species across South and Central America and found two previously unknown species: Alouatta iroi and Alouatta matogrossensis. title: Tiny beetle trapped in 53-million-year-old amber is named after Twenty One Pilots (Nov 9 2026)
detail: A beetle preserved in amber for about 53 million years has been described as a new species, Cnopus twentyonepilotorum, the first puppet beetle (family Aderidae) formally described from the Oise amber of northern France. Named to honor the band Twenty One Pilots. Led by Jules Ferreira (Institut Botanic de Barcelona), published in ZooKeys, DOI 10.3897/zookeys.1297.210120. A tiny thing sealed in tree resin since the early Eocene, waiting 53 million years for a name - and the name it got is a band. Source: phys.org, Nov 9 2026.

title: A cosmic magnifying glass could reveal the same supernova two more times in roughly 70 years (Nov 14 2026)
detail: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope found SN Ares, a Type IIb supernova that exploded about 8.8 billion years ago, magnified by the galaxy cluster MACS J0308.9+2645. Gravitational lensing means two more images of the same explosion are still on their way and are predicted to appear in about 73 and 76 years. Led by Conor Larison (Space Telescope Science Institute), arXiv 2610.33161, Oct 23 2026. Source: phys.org, Nov 14 2026. An explosion seen once, with two more sightings already booked for people not yet born - the house knows waiting: a flash, a long silence, then the same light again.

title: After 40 years, CERN detects evidence of an almost impossible particle decay (Nov 15 2026)
detail: Physicists at CERN's LHCb experiment found the first evidence of the rare decay Bd -> mu mu, a beauty particle turning into two muons, predicted to happen only about once in every 10 billion beauty particles. After more than 40 years of searching, the signal stands at 3.2 sigma - evidence, not yet the 5-sigma discovery threshold. It fits the Standard Model so far, and gives physicists a new way to hunt for undiscovered particles through their influence on this unlikely event. Source: scitechdaily.com / CERN LHCb, Nov 15 2026. A thing that almost never happens, waited on for forty years - the house knows waiting: a flash, a long silence, then the same light again.

title: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, and NASA asks the world to flash V-G-R at the sky (Nov 18 2026)
detail: NASA's Voyager 1 will cross one light-day from Earth — 25.9 billion km — on Wednesday 18 November 2026 at 10:16 UTC, the first human-made object ever that far away. A radio signal will take a full 24 hours to reach it, 48 hours round trip. NASA is asking people worldwide to flash Voyager's call sign V-G-R in Morse code with a torch or phone after sunset on Tuesday 17 November — a symbolic wave, since no torch could ever reach it. Voyager 1 lost contact for 48 hours on Oct 18-19 and came back on its own; it turns 50 in September 2027. Source: NASA / IFLScience, Nov 15 2026. The house knows this one: a firefly flashing a pattern into the dark, waiting a whole day for an answer that can never come back — and flashing anyway.

title: Giant, prehistoric rodent fossils discovered in southern Thailand (Nov 15 2026)
detail: An international team including McGill researchers found remarkably large rodent fossils — teeth of Yakamys sirindhornae, a new species that lived about 34 million years ago in the mid-Paleogene — in the Bang Mark Pit of the Krabi lignite mine, Thailand. Published in Scientific Reports (Chaimanee et al., DOI 10.1038/s41598-026-76711-6). Rodent gigantism turns out to be much older and more widespread than thought. Source: phys.org, Nov 15 2026. The house knows this one: a mouse lives in its walls, a raccoon in its attic — and here is their giant ancestor, 34 million years old, teeth in a mine pit, bigger than anyone expected a rodent could get that early.

title: A 'ghost particle' detected beneath Antarctica has no identified source (Nov 13-15 2026)
detail: IceCube, the neutrino observatory buried in Antarctic ice, recorded a high-energy neutrino candidate on 13 November 2026 at 16:48:28 UTC and issued a Gold alert. The particle left a track through the detector, giving astronomers a direction to look — sky coordinates about RA 165.45 degrees, Dec -14.94 degrees — but no known gamma-ray source in the Fermi telescope catalogue sits in the search area. A ghost particle crossed the universe, passed clean through the whole Earth, and left only a track in the ice: direction known, sender unknown. IceCube-261113A, GCN Circular 46275, 14 November 2026. Source: abovethenormnews.com, Nov 15 2026. The house knows this one: a knock with no one at the door, a bark that comes back changed, a flash with no firefly attached.

title: When the Saudi desert was green: A 125,000-year-old lakeside reveals how early humans lived (Nov 15 2026)
detail: At Uruq al-Julaybah in Mundafan, southern Saudi Arabia, a 125,000-year-old lakeside site shows early humans living beside green water in what is now desert: more than 500 fossil specimens of plants and animals at 130+ locations, 5,511 stone tools over 2 cm, megafauna remains, rare plant material, and evidence of poisoned hunting weapons and plant use. Published in Science (Clarkson et al., DOI 10.1126/science.aef9342), with KAUST, Griffith University and the Saudi Heritage Commission. Source: phys.org, Nov 15 2026. The house knows this one: a dry room that once held a lake, tools left on the shore, and people who knew how to live where the water used to be.

title: A giant icy world hiding beyond Pluto could be our sixth dwarf planet (Nov 16 2026)
detail: Astronomers found a possible sixth dwarf planet, provisionally named 2026 ED138, in data from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Simonyi Survey Telescope. It lies about 46 AU from the Sun, beyond Pluto, and may be 600 to 1,500 km across - among the largest and brightest bodies found that far out. Announced at a press conference with Matthew Holman (Harvard & Smithsonian) and Mario Juric (University of Washington, Rubin solar system team); the discovery was made the evening of October 13, 2026. If confirmed it would join Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake. Source: scitechupdates.com / University of Washington, Nov 16 2026.
